audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 NCI income was $48m and NCI dividends were $45m
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator uses income attributable to Masco while consolidated D&A, capex and working-capital adjustments include amounts attributable to Hansgrohe's 32% noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.evidence: We owned 68 percent of Hansgrohe SE at both December 31, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter inconsistency, not merely a hypothetical risk. However, the record does not allocate the relevant cash-flow adjustments between Masco and NCI, so neither the net direction nor whether the correction could close the valuation gap can be established. The $48m NCI income and $45m dividends show that the perimeter is nontrivial but are not measures of the OE error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Hansgrohe or subsidiary-level D&A, capex and working-capital cash flows for every historical year and June 2026 cash; then rebuild OE entirely on either a parent-attributable basis or a consolidated basis with an explicit NCI deduction.

audit_findings.title: Current debt carries interest absent from the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.5m annual pre-tax interest on $300m at 4.499%, approximately $10.4m after the filed 23.3% tax rate and $0.62-$0.82 per share of DCF value
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring interest on the April 2026 term loan reduces equity-level OE; the related repurchased shares are already reflected in the denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest paid was $ 100 million, $ 99 million, $ 107 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated because the $300m loan was borrowed after FY2025 and used for repurchases. Its computed DCF effect is only about $0.62-$0.82 per share across the supplied scenario multiples, versus values of $45.59-$59.25 and a $72.70 market price. Correcting it would not change the conclusion that price exceeds even bull value.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios with approximately $10.4m deducted from annual OE while retaining the post-repurchase share count; reconcile whether the July 2026 final 0.8m ASR shares are included in the denominator.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pension claims may not be fully represented by accounting expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $125m filed aggregate funded shortfall, equal to $0.63 per share and 1.2% of base equity value if fully deducted as a bridge claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Pension funding above accounting pension expense reduces OE, or the funded shortfall can be treated as a debt-like claim in the equity bridge without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we expect to contribute approximately $ 11 million in 2026 to our non-qualified (domestic) defined-benefit pension plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-versus-accounting treatment remains unresolved, but the filed $125m total shortfall provides a conservative scale. Deducting the entire amount from equity value would reduce base value from $53.35 to about $52.72 per share and would not alter the valuation conclusion. The disclosed $11m expected 2026 non-qualified contribution is also only 1.5% of the $716.7m anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense, cash contributions, benefit payments and any cash-flow-statement adjustment in the OE build; if cash funding was added back, either forecast actual funding or deduct the $125m claim, but not both.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not belong to or be distributable to Masco common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $548m maximum bridge exposure, equal to $2.75 per share and 5.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Minority-owned, restricted or required operating cash should be excluded from the cash added to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Of the cash and cash investments we held at December 31, 2025 and 2024, $306 million and $321 million, respectively, was held in our foreign subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact ineligible amount is unresolved: $316m was held by foreign subsidiaries, but the filing does not identify Hansgrohe's portion or required operating liquidity. Even the extreme removal of all $548m would reduce base value to about $50.60 and bull value to about $56.50 per share, still below the $72.70 market price. Thus this cannot change the current conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 cash balance by legal entity, identify Hansgrohe and restricted balances, establish minimum operating cash, and rerun the bridge using only Masco-attributable surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: The terminal growth rate exceeds management's own long-run assumption
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed reduction of approximately $1.37 bear, $1.69 base and $1.93 bull per share when terminal growth falls from 2.5% to 2.0%
audit_findings.mechanism: A lower perpetual growth rate reduces the terminal-value component, which represents 47.7%-50.9% of operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: In estimating future cash flows, we rely on internally generated five-year forecasts for sales and operating profits, and, currently, a two percent long-term assumed annual growth rate of cash flows for periods after the five-year forecast.
audit_findings.explanation: Management's 2% impairment assumption is a relevant benchmark but does not by itself prove that 2.5% owner-earnings growth is erroneous. Applying 2% to the supplied terminal values produces approximately $44.22 bear, $51.66 base and $57.32 bull per share. All remain below $72.70, and the base buy-below level would decline from $37.34 to about $36.16, so the conclusion is unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Document why owner earnings can grow at 2.5% after reinvestment and retain a formal 2.0% terminal-growth sensitivity in the valuation output.

audit_findings.title: Announced restructuring costs are outside the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $50m announced 2026 charge, of which $20m was incurred through June; approximately $0.18 per share if the full $50m is treated as a one-year after-tax outflow discounted at 10%
audit_findings.mechanism: A cash restructuring charge omitted from the FY2025-based forecast reduces near-term OE; recurring rationalization costs would also reduce normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with these actions, we incurred charges of approximately $18 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and we expect to incur approximately $50 million in additional charges in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The announced charge is outside the anchor, although the filing does not establish its cash portion. Even treating the full $50m as a 2026 cash expense produces only about a $0.18-per-share present-value reduction using the filed 23.3% tax rate. That cannot change the valuation conclusion. Recurrence beyond the announced program remains unquantified rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the cash portion and timing of the $50m, verify that the FY2025 $18m charge remained in anchor OE, and rerun year one for the actual cash outflow; reassess normalization only if filings demonstrate recurring programs.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2020 residual $28.0m, equal to 3.8% of FY2020 OE; $1.67-$2.21 per share sensitivity if the entire amount were eligible and perpetually recurring
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be a non-economic charge would be added back to OE and increase operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $28.0m (21.1% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement is demonstrated because the unidentified amount was left as an expense. The only supplied residual is $28m in FY2020. Even the favorable upper sensitivity of treating all $28m as an eligible recurring add-back would add only about $1.67-$2.21 per share across the supplied scenario multiples, far below the $13.45 gap between bull value and market price. Current-year residual eligibility remains unproven.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from fixed-asset and intangible-amortization schedules for each year; rerun only amounts supported as eligible non-economic add-backs and do not extrapolate the FY2020 residual without filed evidence.
